Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
212 AM EST Sat Nov 7 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 212 AM EST Saturday...

No significant changes with periods of showers expected this weekend 
and into early next week.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 212 AM EST Saturday...

1. A cooler and unsettled pattern is expected this weekend with 
summit level snow possible Sunday morning. 

2. Another round of precipitation expected for the start of the 
work week, with this activity more focused in the favored upslope 
areas of the northern mountains. 

3. Remaining unsettled midweek through the end of the week, 
likely trending cooler by next weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 212 AM EST Saturday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: We await the arrival of showers this morning as a closed 
upper low slowly pivots eastward across the central/eastern Great 
Lakes. Scattered to numerous showers can already be seen out ahead 
of this feature. This area of showers will continue to slowly drift 
east-northeastward as its parent low crosses into southern NY, 
eventually pivoting into our southern sections along a weak inverted 
surface trough. This band of showers will rotate over NY through 
this afternoon before shifting east into VT late today and overnight 
as the upper low spins across southern New England and eventually 
offshore by Sunday morning. Hence expect fairly widespread showers 
through the day and into tonight, then becoming more focused in the 
northern mountains Sunday morning as west-northwest flow develops 
behind the departing low pressure. Snow levels drop to 2200-3200 ft 
as the cold pool moves overhead, and expect some slushy snow 
accumulation will be possible tonight into Sunday morning, generally 
above 2500 ft. Precipitation will wind down Sunday afternoon, with 
some sunshine possible by late in the day. Overall rainfall amounts 
will be a quarter to a half an inch, with locally higher amounts 
possible in the higher terrain. Temperatures will return to somewhat 
seasonal normals today and especially Sunday; highs in the 50s today 
will give way to mid 40s to mid 50s tomorrow. Winds may be a little 
on the breezy side in the Champlain Valley today as north winds get 
funneled down the valley. Strong winds then become more widespread 
on Sunday, though remaining AOB 25 mph or so, with little impact 
expected.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Shortwave ridging briefly builds in behind the departing 
upper low, giving us a short respite from precipitation. However, 
another vigorous upper trough will swing along the international 
border Monday, with another following right in its footsteps on 
Tuesday. Showers will once again develop, though remaining more 
focused in the favored upslope areas of the northern 
Adirondacks/Greens as southwest winds shift to the west and 
eventually northwest. A reinforcing shot of cold air will see snow 
levels falling as low as 1500 ft early Tuesday morning, though the 
bulk of the precipitation will likely have ended by then, limiting 
potential snow accumulation. Total precipitation amounts will be a 
quarter of an inch or less through Monday night, with another tenth 
of two possible on Tuesday. Both days will see temperatures close to 
or just a bit above normal, generally in the mid 40s to low 50s.

KEY MESSAGE 3: The large Hudson Bay low will continue to dominate the 
weather across our region, bringing multiple shortwaves into the 
weekend. A Shortwave pushes through on Tuesday bringing valley rain 
showers and some chances for snow to the upper terrain locations, 
mainly above 3000 feet AGL. That snow level should drop overnight 
and give Mt. Mansfield its first chance of seeing 1" of snow, which 
would be the latest ever on record, breaking the record of Nov 9th 
set in 1956 and 1985. While things remain unsettled the rest of the 
week, models are keying in on significant closed low swinging down 
through the Mid-Atlantic region and then up the coastline, bringing 
several shots of rain and rain/snow mix into the weekend. This 
system will definitely bare closer monitoring as the week 
progresses.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z SATURDAY THROUGH WEDNESDAY/...
Through 06Z Sunday...IFR ceilings are expected at BTV and EFK
to start the period. Other stations will likely go from VFR to 
low MVFR and IFR within a few hours at most terminals, generally
between 07-13Z. Low ceilings will prevail for the rest of the 
day, though rises of several hundred feet are likely. Areas of 
mist and drizzle will also accompany these ceilings, especially 
at BTV, SLK and EFK. Scattered showers will move through 
later in the morning, with more organized rain possible in the 
afternoon. While this rain by itself will likely not be enough 
to significantly reduce the visibility, it will likely combine 
with the mist/drizzle and there will be periods of MVFR 
visibility. Winds will generally be under 10 KT and 
northerly/northeasterly, or light and variable.

Outlook...

Sunday: Mainly VFR, with local IFR possible. Chance RA, Chance
SHRA.
Sunday Night: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Monday: Mainly MVFR, with local IFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Monday Night: Mainly MVFR, with areas VFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday: Mainly MVFR, with areas VFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Tuesday Night: Mainly MVFR, with areas VFR possible. Chance SHRA.
Veterans Day: Mainly MVFR, with local VFR possible. Chance SHRA.

&&
